query: The Last Bout Three down, and the cellar has gone quiet. {~The ring's own champion steps in: a duellist the academy expelled, who hasn't lost down here in a year.|The bookmaker himself takes off his coat. His wand was in it all along, and the old hands step back from the chalk.|A girl in a borrowed cloak steps in, a runaway from Thornwick. Her shadow moves a moment after she does, and the old hands start betting against you.} {flag(ring_last_standing): Last standing: win this and the night is yours.|Win, and the cellar will talk about you for a term. Or go while you can still walk.} Fight the last bout {~The champion's ward breaks at last, and the cellar stamps until dust comes down from the boathouse floor. You go home with a purse you can barely lift.|He reads your next spell out of your head every time, so you cast the one you hadn't thought of. He goes down laughing and pays you from his own coat.|You hit the shadow, not the girl, and she yields, grinning, and buys you a drink you can't hold. You walk home sore and rich and famous in one cellar.} {~The champion ends it in one spell, and you understand why the academy wanted them gone. You wake on the steps with your night's winnings and a long walk.|The bookmaker casts things the library keeps chained, and wins clean. You crawl up the steps holding your purse and your ribs.|You can't tell the girl from her shadow, and the wrong one hits you. The crowd is so loud the prefects must hear it.} Take the purse and go {~You bow out with three wins and a heavy purse. The champion nods: next time.|You don't fight the man who sets the odds, and knows your thoughts. You take your winnings before he can change his mind.|You look at the runaway's shadow and decide three is plenty.}
